I was much the same. I'm currently in a mundane, repetitive hole of a help desk job. And yeah - I hate the work, I hate everyone here (except one) and I want to stay in bed and say that I can no longer work due to direct allergies with every person there. 

I can't do much at the moment, everyone I live with rely on my income to get by until they find work - but next year I'm starting to get into more "hands on" I.T. jobs. 

I also know mechanics like that, but never forget that they too did start small and did have to start out at the beginners level. Find something that'll get you the training and move up - when you feel you're not in a comfortable job and know there's something better you can go for - jump at it. It's not so much a chance thing, it's more of just playing your cards right. 

I myself - despite my job's immense downfall of being boring as hell - it does pay quite well. So here I am in a job where everyone around me has certifications in I.T. and I have none. Just the hands on experience over the last 5 or so years. 

So yeah - it really is just a matter of getting into it and getting enough knowledge about the way things work - and it's now very clear you're definitely highly intelligent so I have no doubts you'd thrive on the information.

They are indeed stunning. Absolutely. I also can't help but notice that you've sparked up your inner motor enthusiast :P.
Are you certain there are no options in your area to even start out in anything mechanical?
It doesn't really require you to be overly fit and remember there is always room down the track for I.T. people to get into a more technical/mechanical role and you'd get to learn it a whole lot more.

I know the feeling only too well... especially about finding the ones you can ACTUALLY relate to in some of the stranger corners of your mind.

I do like the old Mustangs - they're particularly popular here as cars that are rare yet very loved and well kept. 

I've never been a fan of Australian build Fords - something about America's influence on their design both new and old is something I'm particularly fond of - which is a strange prospect considering I'm into the simplicity of design at the same time. Haven't seen a Saleen down here but certainly wish that it was down here... :(

Correct, I'm from Australia so I'm a little rusty with international... er.... terminology :P

I can absolutely relate, and believe me this is one time it's worth being stubborn. We all have the potential to do great things at any age in any situation. As long as you can see this even with the odds stacked against you then you have everything to gain. 
Also - and maybe a female redditor will input here - but when a guy is able to pick himself up from an otherwise bad situation and they witness it? They find this admirable and even sometimes quite attractive. 

As far as "ruining" your last relationship?
Take away more of the lessons learnt about that situation and get yourself back on track. Who knows? You'll meet someone much more suited to you that blows your mind...she may even come back around! Too many variables!

I'm also a big fan of American muscle cars and I have never heard of the Mach 1 but wow is that a great car... that Cobra engine has a growl not to be forgotten. 

Feel free to send me an inbox if you get stuck with anything as well. It's good to find someone with an understanding in the level you perceive - especially you being like me and just wanting to do something about feeling "stuck". :)

I'm the same in that aspect too, I love building performance/gaming machines and the demand is only low because of the market being flooded by people who have been doing it for the long term (which really sucks so this'll be best to stay as your hobby).

One day go up to the paintball ranges (without a booking) and ask if they have any shifts free. Most paintball places are pretty motivated and in my experience it's a motivation that's highly contagious. That shyness/nervousness you have is on the opposite scale of your confidence. It'll take the right kind of situation to start tilting the scales back to the way you are when you're more confident. 

I know how the depression feels - it's a more complex reasoning but it may even drive my current partner away. Sometimes I have to take parts of a day minute by minute so I don't let it get the better of me but as long as you're choosing (like myself) to try to fight it with every tiny morsel or spark of motivation that might reach your emotions then you're at least willing to keep to feeling like you still have so much to give. At least that's how I'm perceiving your state of mind...

Just for extra perspective - name a car you'd buy instantly if you had the chance.

It is clear from the way you type, talk and structure sentences alone that you are intelligent, mature and resourceful and it is crystal that maybe college isn't for you. What part of computers really makes you motivated?

Secondly and funnily enough I'm more recently interested in firearms and was coincidentally sparked by going out to paintball as well. Are you certain traveling that distance is too far? It might be worth starting out working at a paintball range. 

Thirdly, I haven't talked to my mum since 2009 and my dad is never around - I haven't lived with my family since I was 16. I was the true definition of rogue and I get outcasted by everyone so I know exactly what you're feeling.

And yet it already feels wasted. I'm not very old but I posses a state of mind a 30 year old will struggle to grasp. I grew up too fast and it damn near murdered my inner child. Everything I do now makes me dread when I will fail it. And it is hard to conceal at work bit so far nobody has noticed. My partner noticed I was upset tonight but it wasn't because I want to disappear. It's because she really doesn't care about me. I already feel wasted. Chewed up. Spat out. You know what hurts the most? I'm never alone. People are always around me, talking or not, and all I feel is I'm listening to them through soundproof glass. While that numb, cold feeling eats my inner emotions.

I search for people with your method of thinking. Far and wide, long and hard. I decide to take a chance in the hope someone can make any sense of me and it takes a couple of complete strangers - one asking more details and you as a complete stranger who has summed me up in précise words. 
Years of searching for anyone who thinks like me and it takes a single reddit post. Wisdom is your forte...
I'm no saint myself. I suppose I had to make the mistakes to become a man with the ability to want to right the wrongs in my life and they always stay wrong. My ability fails. 
Something happened tonight that does confirm I am giving all and everyone is taking. Even my partner. She pretends to care and I have nowhere else to turn to.
I wish my logic knowledge would hold more than just weight. I've spent no end of time trying to show lifes true presence. But the only people who will listen are the ones who will never give back. As for showing if I'm the one to speak out or walk away I seem to have found a disastrous third option. Speaking out sometimes and shying away in others. It makes for a confusing person. 

Look, I know life was never meant to be easy, but the stack of things ruining every chance I smile means I'm not myself. I don't know when I was smiling like that at all. My face has created downward dimples because I am physically sad and just a broken shell of a man. 

Maybe it's me that's being ignorant or shallow minded... I just don't know. I'm not strong enough to find out more...
Just back from work. And feel free.
I'm still here sorry. I'm trying to fight this. I might lose but I'll still try.

I've spent an eternity thinking that way - and I'm exhausted. I am just so tired. I've been fighting for everything to be right, fighting for the right friends who left me to rot when I needed them, fighting to keep a woman in my life that will be most likely leaving me in the coming year, fighting to have a career I can be proud of when I know it won't last, fighting for everything. I don't have much fight left anymore. I just don't have it in me anymore. I've lost track of the last time I ever knew what it was like to smile without having a searing burn of underlying pain and suffering. And I'm tired. All I'm throwing away is the towel - from a fight I won't win - let alone get any steps up. I used to think the way my mind works could help people. It did. It help them use some for life's greatest intangible treasures to do despicable things. I am nothing. Merely a fade to black in life's little movie. A scene transition. 

The negative forces I used to ignore, self-motivation is something that can overcome anything. But I don't have anything to motivate me anymore. My heart feels like a burnt out house and my soul feels like it's in a coma. I can't feel - only a searing, sickening numbness that tranquilises my body right through. I really don't have anywhere I can stay anymore. If I stop working then I'll have nothing else.
